clue.text: For European this is a handy American port

definitions.text: For European this is a handy
definitions.meaning: in German, and so for many Europeans, a Handy is the pocket phone Americans call a cell
a city on the Gulf coast of Alabama with a busy harbour

explanation.surface: A traveller is told that some American harbour town is convenient for visitors from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handy' looks like the English adjective 'convenient', but it is the German word for a cellphone, so the first half is a cryptic way of describing the British phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the British word for a cellphone, and the Alabama seaport of the same name.

clue.text: A barrel's broken in temper, so repair damage

indicators.note: broken in means forced inside, so the barrel goes into the word for temper

parts.note: a mood is a fit of temper
a keg is a small barrel

explanation.surface: A cask smashed in a fit of rage, so someone must pay for the damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' suggests an anagram, but the letters of A KEG go into MOOD unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: To make good is an idiom for compensating for loss or putting right damage.

clue.text: Lonely female's mislaid hat

indicators.note: mislaid means lost, so the letter for female drops out of the longer word

parts.note: bereft means left lonely and desolate
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A forlorn woman has lost her hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A beret is a round, flat, brimless cap, a kind of hat.

clue.text: Unprofessional to gamble

definitions.meaning: not of the clergy or other profession, amateur
to stake money on a bet

explanation.definitionFit: Lay describes a non-specialist, and to lay a bet is to wager money.

clue.text: Fish, cheaper variety, served by sous-chef for starters

indicators.note: served by places the opening letter beside the shuffled fodder, ahead of it
for starters asks for the opening letter of the kitchen word sous-chef
a variety of the word cheaper is a different arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A restaurant offers a fish dish at a cheaper price, brought out by the junior chef as an appetiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' and 'sous-chef' set a kitchen scene, so 'variety' reads as a range of dishes; it is the anagram signal, giving EAPERCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea perch is any of various marine fishes resembling the freshwater perch, such as the bass.

clue.text: Like mournful poem, say, penned by writer at start of century

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the writer's name holds the abbreviation for say

parts.note: Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb
eg (for example) means say

indicators.note: at start of takes the opening letter of century

explanation.surface: An essayist at the turn of the century writes something in the style of a lament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is EG, a crossword convention; ELIA is Charles Lamb's pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem, and elegiac is the adjective relating to such verse.

clue.text: On top of a mango tree, mushy soft fruit

indicators.note: On top of places the letter above the anagram in this down entry

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft

indicators.note: mushy suggests the letters of a mango tree mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A soft, overripe fruit sits on a mango tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mushy' rearranges A MANGO TREE into OMEGRANATE, which goes under P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pomegranate is a round fruit with tough skin and many juicy seeds.

clue.text: Quits after editor's introduced new plans

indicators.note: introduced means put inside, so the editor's letters go into the word for quits

parts.note: resigns means quits a job
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Someone walks out after an editor brings in fresh schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' only links. 'new plans' is a plural noun, matching the answer read as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Redesigns as a plural noun are revised designs, that is, new plans for something.

clue.text: Strap is hard to adjust

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to alter is to adjust

explanation.surface: A strap is difficult to adjust.
explanation.definitionFit: A halter is a strap or rope for leading an animal, and also a neck strap on a top.

clue.text: Put pressure on head of CID to stop dodgy deal

indicators.note: on places the letter for pressure above the rest in this down entry

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the initial goes inside the jumbled word
dodgy suggests the letters of deal rearranged
head of takes the first letter of CID

explanation.surface: Detectives lean on a suspect to halt a shady transaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' makes LAED of DEAL; 'to stop' puts C into it, giving LACED. CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed is a past tense of place, which means put something somewhere.

clue.text: In Kentucky waste you'll find stray dog

indicators.note: In places the word for stray inside the state's postal abbreviation

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky
to err is to stray from the right path
to blue money is old British slang for squandering it

explanation.surface: Somewhere in the Kentucky wilds a lost dog turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' as a verb, to spend money recklessly, is British slang (also spelt blow).
explanation.definitionFit: The Kerry blue is an Irish terrier breed with a soft blue-grey coat.

clue.text: Gong finally sounded in middle of dinner?

indicators.note: in middle of puts the picked letter into the centre of the word for dinner

parts.note: a dinner is a meal

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word sounded

explanation.surface: A dinner gong rings out at last halfway through the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gong' looks like the dinner gong of the surface, but it is British slang for a medal or decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British informal slang for a decoration or award, especially a medal.

clue.text: Make excellent start

parts.note: to make somewhere is to get there, as in get home
cracking is British informal for excellent

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin superbly.
explanation.definitionFit: To get cracking is an idiom meaning to start work promptly and energetically.

clue.text: Prepared money for circulation

parts.note: the ready is British slang for cash
to can mean for, as in a key to the door
roll means turning round and round, circulating

explanation.surface: Cash is prepared for putting into circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' meaning cash in hand is British slang (also 'readies').
explanation.definitionFit: Ready to roll is an idiom for being fully prepared to start.

clue.text: Book into posh establishment

indicators.note: into signals the letters lie buried inside the phrase posh establishment

explanation.surface: A reservation is made at a smart hotel or club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb meaning reserve; it is a noun, the novel by H. Rider Haggard.
explanation.definitionFit: Rider Haggard's adventure novel about the immortal queen Ayesha is titled with this pronoun.

clue.text: Cultivated land yielding golden vegetable

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
chard is a leafy vegetable related to beet

explanation.surface: Farmland produces a crop of gilded greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yielding' simply links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is an area of ground planted and tended with fruit trees, so cultivated land.

clue.text: American newspaper article containing no end of prejudice

indicators.note: containing means the newspaper word wraps around the shortened word

parts.note: a column is a regular article in a newspaper

indicators.note: no end of means the final letter is removed from the synonym

parts.note: bias means prejudice

explanation.surface: A US newspaper piece is full of bigotry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' can mean of the USA; Columbia is the poetic name for America, so the adjective fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Columbian means relating to America, from Columbia, its poetic personification.

clue.text: Accuse person in custody

definitions.meaning: to bring a formal accusation against someone
someone placed in another's care, such as a ward or pupil

explanation.definitionFit: To charge is to accuse formally, and a charge is also a person entrusted to someone's care.

clue.text: Passengers ultimately facing trouble at airport tarry, maybe

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the final letter of Passengers

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
Orly is one of the airports of Paris

explanation.surface: Travellers end up having problems at the airport, perhaps a delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tarry' looks like the verb 'linger', but it means like a tar (an old word for a sailor); 'maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A tar is slang for a sailor, so tarry here is an example of seamanlike behaviour.

clue.text: Exaggerate malfunction

definitions.meaning: to overstate or make much of something
of a machine, to fail to work properly

explanation.definitionFit: To play up a point is to emphasise it unduly, and a device that plays up is misbehaving.

clue.text: First immerse in water smooth cut timber

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the final letter comes off the word for smooth

parts.note: to press clothes is to smooth them
oak is a timber

explanation.surface: Before treating sawn wood, plane it smooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First immerse in water' is the whole definition, though 'First' looks like an ordering instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To presoak something is to soak it beforehand, before washing or cooking it.

clue.text: Port area featured in news broadcast in South Africa

indicators.note: in puts the whole assembled piece between the letters for South Africa
featured in places the letter for area inside the rearranged word
broadcast suggests the word news scattered about into a new order

explanation.surface: A harbour region appears in a news report from South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns NEWS into WNSE; 'featured in' puts A inside it, giving WANSE, and 'in' puts that between S and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a coastal city and seaport in South Wales.

clue.text: Jewish community group in which there's high tension at length

indicators.note: at places the length letter at the end
in which there's says the group holds the next two letters inside

parts.note: a set is a group
T is the abbreviation for tension

explanation.surface: A group where emotions run high for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: A shtetl was a small Jewish town or village in eastern Europe.

clue.text: Supplier of milk to children

parts.note: the dairy animal as named in nursery speech, from the sound it makes

explanation.walkthrough: 'to children' says the word is children's talk: the animal is named for its noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Children's name for a cow, the animal that supplies milk.

clue.text: Law man's expression of surprise, meeting spy master

definitions.note: read as Law man is: a scientist with a law named after him

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A policeman gasps when he meets the head of an intelligence agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Law man' suggests a policeman; it is the German physicist whose law relates voltage, current and resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Ohm formulated the law that current equals voltage divided by resistance.

clue.text: Duke of York's men didn't get this old

definitions.text: Duke of York's men didn't get this
definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme the Grand Old Duke of York marched his ten thousand men up to the top of the hill and down again, never beyond it

explanation.walkthrough: The British nursery rhyme 'The Grand Old Duke of York' has the soldiers marched up a hill and back down, so they never got beyond the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Being past the peak of life is an idiom for being too old for something.

clue.text: Confirm arrangement, writing single note to family members

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral, is a single one
N is an abbreviation for note, as in a footnote reference
kin are family members

explanation.surface: A single footnote addressed to relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' is the abbreviation N, not a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: To ink something in is to fill a pencilled entry with ink, confirming an arrangement in writing.

clue.text: Type of fabric, check one? Not so

parts.note: CH is the chess notation for check
I is the Roman numeral one
no denies that something is so

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a patterned cloth is a check, and is told it isn't.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check' looks like a fabric pattern, fitting the surface, but it is the chess abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a twilled cotton cloth used for trousers, so a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Australian about to visit Korea but reorganised

indicators.note: to visit puts the abbreviation for about inside the rearranged letters
reorganised says the letters of Korea and but are put into a new order

parts.note: C, for circa, is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: An Australian goes on a trip to Korea, but the itinerary is changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reorganised' gives OUTBAKER; the K comes from Korea, not from its usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbacker is a person who lives in the remote Australian interior, so an Australian.

clue.text: Old man turns up regularly creating trouble

indicators.note: turns up means the letters are read upwards, backwards in this down entry
regularly takes alternate letters of the words Old man

explanation.surface: An elderly man shows up now and then, causing a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes ODA from OLD MAN, and 'turns up' turns it to ADO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss and bother, a disturbance or trouble.

clue.text: We'll bottle popular red and white in great quantity?

indicators.note: bottle means hold inside, so the first word encloses the word for popular

parts.note: the contraction is taken as just its first part, the letters of we
in means fashionable or popular
lake is a crimson pigment, a type of red

explanation.surface: A promise to bottle a well-liked red and white wine in bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' looks like part of the wine description; it is the pigment LAKE. The question mark admits that a surplus of white is only one example of the stockpile.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine lake is the large surplus of unsold wine built up under the EU farm policy, a great quantity of it.

clue.text: Sauce for fish always served at noon?

indicators.note: served at places the word for always after the morning word

parts.note: morning lasts until noon, so the morn ends then; the question mark admits the stretch
ay, or aye, is an old word for always or ever

explanation.surface: A fish sauce that is always on the lunchtime menu.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits noon is only the end of the morning, a loose fit the blogger also noted.
explanation.definitionFit: Mornay is a cheese-flavoured white sauce often served with fish or eggs.
